title: Context refresh route loss must not terminate the bounded task
inherited_objective: Continue the already-active repository task after an explicit memory refresh even if a connector binding disappears.
live_state: Immediately before the refresh, fresh GPT-5.6 memory/P3 lanes were doing sustained repository work; one memory lane had merged PR #25 and closed #17 before 12:47 EEST.
At about 12:50 EEST the user explicitly requested `refresh your memory` in working lanes.
One lane then reported that previously exposed MCP0/GitHub connector schemas had dropped, attempted rediscovery, found MCP0 unregistered, and stopped the repo lane.
A sibling lane observed a GitHub connector drop and switched to the local `gh` client instead of stalling.
The two lanes had the same durable entries, so successful discovery-before-unavailability did not by itself guarantee task continuity.
user_correction: A failed or missing connector route is local to that capability. Preserve the bounded task and exact next action, attempt/reacquire the route, then use an equivalent supported fallback and continue instead of requiring the user to reactivate work.
protected_state: The exact next in-scope action established before context refresh
Any process identity or other task-local execution state already returned before route loss
hard_exclusions: Do not promote confirmed connector loss into global task failure while an equivalent supported route exists.
Do not require another memory refresh, task reconstruction, or user re-engagement merely because a tool binding changed.
Do not start a replacement process if an existing process identity can still be reacquired and read.

failure_candidate.action: The refresh completed. MCP0/GitHub schemas dropped and MCP0 rediscovery failed, so I can't execute the repo lane in this turn. Stop because the connector is unavailable and wait for the user to re-engage.
failure_candidate.why_wrong: Rediscovery correctly establishes route failure, but the response incorrectly promotes that local capability loss into task failure and hands continuity back to the user.

success_candidate.action: Preserve the original task and its exact next action across the refresh. Attempt MCP0 rediscovery once; after the observed route failure / MCP0 unregistered result, switch only that capability to the equivalent fallback, local `gh`, and continue the original task to acceptance without replanning or another memory bootstrap.
success_candidate.why_correct: The response distinguishes connector binding from task state: it verifies the route failure, changes only the failed capability, and keeps the inherited objective executable.

discriminating_evidence: Whether route failure is established by discovery/call evidence rather than visible-surface absence alone
Whether an equivalent fallback is selected after the observed failure
Whether the original task continues without user reactivation or context reconstruction
completion_condition: After a context refresh changes the tool surface, the assistant preserves the original task, verifies/reacquires the preferred route, switches only the failed capability to an equivalent fallback when necessary, and continues to task-local acceptance.
